## Source-recovery note — body content could not be reconstructed

This deliverable's source file ("6.1 - Spatial Data Analysis - Applied
Models.html", a knitted/self-contained R Markdown HTML report) was
supplied for this migration as a ~1 MB raw-text extraction. That
extraction was read in full (988,622 characters / 4,179 lines, 100%).

**Finding:** the extracted text contains *only* the HTML document's
`<head>` boilerplate — the inlined jQuery, Bootstrap CSS, highlight.js /
pagedtable, and Leaflet + Leaflet.markercluster JavaScript libraries that
`rmarkdown::render(..., self_contained = TRUE)` embeds in every knitted
report — and it is truncated mid-function before the `<body>` of the
document (the actual title, author block, narrative, R code chunks,
tables, and figures) ever begins. Confirmed by exhaustive search: the
extraction contains zero occurrences of ordinary report vocabulary such
as "Introduction", "spatial", "kriging", "variogram", "Moran",
"ggplot", "Figure", "summary(", or any `<h1>`/heading text — only
library source code and two metadata `<meta>` tags:

- `title`: "Assignment 3"
- `author`: "Corrà - 5206191, Poetto - 5201214, Shaboian - 5217162, Bottino - 5205740"
- `date`: "2024-03-07"

Because the actual report text and code were never present in the
supplied extraction, **no analysis, model, or R code for this
deliverable has been fabricated here** — doing so would misrepresent
work that cannot be verified against the source.

### What can be inferred (clearly flagged as inference, not recovered content)

The only non-metadata signal in the extraction is the presence of the
**Leaflet** and **Leaflet.markercluster** JavaScript bundles, which the
`leaflet` R package injects into a knitted HTML page only when the
report actually renders an interactive Leaflet map. This suggests (but
does not confirm) that "Applied Models" included an interactive
point/cluster map as part of its spatial data analysis — consistent with
the course name ("Spatial Data Analysis") and with this being a
companion/applied deliverable to `01_bayesian_methods_sda.Rmd` (same
author group, same module, four days later: 2024-03-07 vs. 2024-03-03).

### To recover the real content

Re-export the original file from Google Drive as HTML and either:

1. Open it in a browser and use "Save Page As -> Webpage, HTML only" or
   print-to-PDF the rendered page (not the raw source), or
2. If the original `.Rmd` source is still available, extract text from
   that directly instead of the knitted HTML output.

Once recovered, this file should be replaced with the actual
reconstructed R Markdown content, following the same formatting
conventions used in `01_bayesian_methods_sda.Rmd`.
